newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE LOOK TO TRI-NATIONS SPOT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE LOOK TO TRI-NATIONS SPOT.

text.p: France would like to be part of the southern hemisphere Tri-Nations rugby union competition to test themselves regularly against Australia, South Africa and New Zealand, French captain Abdel Benazzi said on Wednesday.
"We want to be part of this grand slam (Tri-series) you have and we want more games in the southern hemisphere," Benazzi told reporters.
The 54-test veteran said the Five Nations champions had a 50-percent chance of beating Australia in Saturday's first test at the Sydney Football Stadium.
"This year we proved we are a good team in the northern hemisphere and now we arrive here with a big challenge," said Benazzi, 28, who plays either flanker or number eight.
"They (Australia) want to play good rugby, they want to try many players. We also have a big ambition to play good rugby and I think we are 50-50 against Wallabies.
"We want to continue with the same performance of the (Five Nations) Grand Slam this year," he said.
Benazzi said he felt an additional responsibility as captain on tour because his teammates had little experience of Australian conditions.
"We have many young players and it's only me who has been to Australia before. This team is now my responsibility," said Benazzi, who played in France's losing touring side in 1990.
France have beaten Queensland, ACT, and Victoria in tour matches since arriving in Australia 10 days ago.
But those performances offered few clues as to their prospects against Australia because both Queensland and ACT fielded weakened sides in the absence of their test players.
Wallaby coach Greg Smith called his squad together last Wednesday in preparation for the test series.
The second and final test will be staged at Ballymore in Brisbane on June 28.
France are expected to name their line-up on Thursday for the first test.
